name: Futurism
summary: Futurism, as a political current, grew out of Marinetti's 1909 Italian art movement. It celebrated speed, machines, youth, violence and war, rejected the past and its institutions, and married this to intense Italian nationalism. In politics it formed a short-lived party in 1918, merged into early Fascism as its anti-monarchist, anti-clerical left wing, and remained loosely tied to the regime until 1944.
scope: The Italian Futurism of F. T. Marinetti, 1909-1944, with weight on the 1909 manifesto and the 1918 Futurist Political Party program. Russian Futurism (many of whose members embraced communism) and later 'futurist' or technoprogressive usages are excluded.

sources.usedFor: 1918 program: technical youth government, anti-monarchy, anti-clerical, progressive tax, no inheritance, volunteer army, expansionism.

universal-healthcare.rationale: 1918 program mixes state-funded child-rearing with little on health; not addressed, so split.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The program backed strikes and worker education but set no wage floor; not addressed.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Futurists wanted a technocratic, state-steered modernization and scorned bourgeois liberal passivity; inferred, not stated.

public-ownership.rationale: Not addressed; early program was statist in tone but proposed no nationalization list.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The 1918 program called for progressive taxation and abolition of inheritance.

unions-good.rationale: The program backed freedom to strike, but Futurism later accepted Fascist syndicates; split.

property-fundamental.rationale: The program proposed abolishing inheritance and Georgist land reform, so property is not sacrosanct.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Not addressed; no stated stance on corporate regulation.

cut-welfare.rationale: Not addressed; the program included state-funded child-rearing but is silent on welfare cuts.

worker-ownership.rationale: Futurism was about nation and youth, not worker ownership; inferred.

surveillance-ok.rationale: The program called for abolishing the political police, though Futurists accepted Fascist rule later; inferred.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed; Futurists favoured provocation and bohemian excess but made no program statement.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: A movement exalting provocation, insult and 'the punch and the slap' would resist speech limits; inferred.

strong-leader.rationale: Marinetti backed Mussolini and the program wanted a small youth council replacing parliament and Senate.

state-harmful.rationale: Futurism was nationalist and statist, seeking a technical government, not abolition of the state.

limit-guns.rationale: Militarist glorification of violence implies opposition to disarmament; gun control not addressed.

empower-police-military.rationale: The manifesto glorifies militarism and Futurists campaigned for war and Italian military power.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed; the program taxed 'free love' and Marinetti scorned conventional morality; split.

decide-locally.rationale: The 1918 program wanted bureaucratic decentralization but a strong national, expansionist state; net mildly against.

rehabilitation.rationale: The program called for prison reform; the direction is inferred.

traditional-family.rationale: The program proposed abolishing marriage, with state-raised children, while the 1909 manifesto attacked tradition.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not addressed; Futurism attacked marriage itself and was masculinist.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed in sources opened; split.

more-religion-public.rationale: The 1918 program denounced parasitical clericalism, although Marinetti accepted the Church's influence in the 1930s.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Futurism was nationalist and Marinetti accepted Fascist racial policy after 1938; not a Futurist theme, inferred.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed; the movement's positions on sex were essentialist in tone.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Futurists were intensely nationalist and claimed Futurism as Italian, but rejected inherited tradition, so the answer is modest.

gradual-change.rationale: Futurism rejected the past and established institutions outright.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not addressed in the sources opened.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Nationalist and expansionist; international bodies did not exist in its early period; inferred.

free-trade.rationale: Futurism's manifestos and 1918 program say nothing on this, so the answer is left neutral as not addressed.

nation-first.rationale: Nationalism and patriotism are glorified in the manifesto and defined the movement.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: War was glorified for national and aesthetic reasons, not human rights; inferred.

open-borders.rationale: A nationalist, expansionist movement; open borders would contradict it.

limit-growth.rationale: Futurism celebrated industry, speed and the machine.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic; its celebration of industry implies resistance.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: It exalted technology and speed, though mainly as aesthetic and national renewal, not problem-solving.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from its enthusiasm for new technology.

revolution-justified.rationale: The manifesto exalts aggression and destructive gestures, and Futurists pushed war and militant action.

experts-over-public.rationale: The program wanted technical government, though it was run by a youth council.

central-planning.rationale: Futurism's manifestos and 1918 program say nothing on this, so the answer is left neutral as not addressed.

socialized-markets.rationale: Futurism's manifestos and 1918 program say nothing on this, so the answer is left neutral as not addressed.

land-value-tax.rationale: The program proposed Henry George-style land reform but not a single land tax; split.

tax-inheritance.rationale: The 1918 program called for abolishing inheritance.

basic-income.rationale: Futurism's manifestos and 1918 program say nothing on this, so the answer is left neutral as not addressed.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Marinetti urged industrial, militarized development, but no investment policy was stated; inferred.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Not addressed beyond land reform for veterans.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Futurism's manifestos and 1918 program say nothing on this, so the answer is left neutral as not addressed.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Futurists in the Fascist era worked within syndicalist structures, but this was not a Futurist doctrine.

one-party-rule.rationale: Marinetti founded a party and joined Fascism, but left in 1920 over its accommodation; split.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Opposition to the monarchy was a core demand of the 1918 program.

democracy-best.rationale: The program replaced parliament and Senate with a youth council, while the 1909 text rejects tradition and accepted Fascist rule.

direct-votes.rationale: The program had a directly elected council but no stated referendums.

workers-councils.rationale: Nationalist; wanted a youth technical council, not workers' councils.

natural-rulers.rationale: Youth and the heroic few were elevated; inferred.

political-violence-never.rationale: The manifesto glorifies violence and 'the destructive gesture'.

war-builds-character.rationale: War is called 'the world's only hygiene'.

separate-church-state.rationale: Anti-clericalism was in the 1918 program, though Marinetti softened later.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Futurism's manifestos and 1918 program say nothing on this, so the answer is left neutral as not addressed.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Futurism was cultural-nationalist; Marinetti went along with 1938 racial laws but this was not defining.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Fascists and Futurists held that nation outranks class, though Futurism glorified conflict.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Abolishing inheritance is egalitarian but the movement elevated heroic elites; inferred.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Marinetti covered the Libya war and volunteered for the Ethiopian war.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Not addressed; heroic national sacrifice was valued over self-interest.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Patriotic duty and sacrifice are exalted; inferred.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Celebrated machine and industrial city over nature.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: It celebrated the industrial city and machine age.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Speed, technology and disruption of the old order are central.

human-enhancement.rationale: Marinetti envisioned replacing food with pills and the machine-man; inferred.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic; it favoured technical government but by humans.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Futurism's manifestos and 1918 program say nothing on this, so the answer is left neutral as not addressed.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Not addressed; Futurism was a strongly programmatic ideology of action.

means-match-ends.rationale: Futurism's manifestos and 1918 program say nothing on this, so the answer is left neutral as not addressed.

collective-farming.rationale: Land reform for veterans suggests small holders; inferred.

harm-principle.rationale: It exalted aggression and a statist nationalism; inferred.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Futurism's manifestos and 1918 program say nothing on this, so the answer is left neutral as not addressed.

conscription.rationale: The program proposed replacing compulsory service with a voluntary army.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Futurism's manifestos and 1918 program say nothing on this, so the answer is left neutral as not addressed.

state-as-business.rationale: It wanted technical government but not market-style.

media-academia-power.rationale: Not addressed; it attacked academies and critics as cultural power but made no claim about political power.

total-state.rationale: Futurists wanted Futurism as state art but the regime did not accept it; split.

single-common-good.rationale: Futurism's manifestos and 1918 program say nothing on this, so the answer is left neutral as not addressed.

school-vouchers.rationale: Futurism's manifestos and 1918 program say nothing on this, so the answer is left neutral as not addressed.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Futurism's manifestos and 1918 program say nothing on this, so the answer is left neutral as not addressed.

economic-freedom.rationale: Its program favoured a state-led technical government and nationalist mobilisation over economic liberty; inferred.

reason-over-faith.rationale: It prized instinct, intuition and speed over reason.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Futurism's manifestos and 1918 program say nothing on this, so the answer is left neutral as not addressed.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Futurism's manifestos and 1918 program say nothing on this, so the answer is left neutral as not addressed.

class-collaboration.rationale: Program offered patriotic education to the proletariat and nation over class.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The manifesto vows to destroy museums, libraries and academies.

positive-liberty.rationale: Not addressed; the 1918 program had state-funded child-rearing but Futurism prized individual daring more than material guarantees.

dominated-front.rationale: Inferred from its Italian nationalism and expansionism; it sought Italian supremacy rather than a common front of dominated countries.

workers-nation.rationale: Inferred from its intense nationalism and later merger with Fascism, which organised workers along national lines.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Split: the manifesto scorns woman and the 1918 era Futurism was male-heroic, yet the movement also attacked the traditional family and domestic role; inferred.

ban-interest.rationale: Inferred: the program attacked inheritance and landed privilege but proposed no ban on lending.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Inferred: Futurism was nationalist and expansionist but did not centre on racial classification, and Marinetti was no core supporter of racial segregation law.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Inferred: it framed politics around nation and youth rather than class and rejected the Marxist analysis.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Inferred from the Futurist cult of machines, speed and industry, which implies abundant cheap fuel; no energy policy was stated.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Inferred from the movement's aggressive Italian nationalism and expansionism; immigration itself was not a program issue.

elite-replacement.rationale: Not addressed; the movement's targets were the monarchy, clergy and passeist elites, not a migration plot. Inferred.

proportional-representation.rationale: The 1918 program wanted parliament replaced by a government of technical youth, so a party-list system is not a Futurist aim; inferred.

national-mission.rationale: Futurism glorified Italian expansion and the 1918 program was expansionist, but it spoke of Italian primacy more than of exporting a form of government.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The manifesto scorned woman and Futurism mocked feminism, though the 1918 program backed votes for women; adherents would deny a structural bias against women.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The 1918 program attacked parliament, monarchy and the old political class as backward, and aimed to replace them with youth.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Not addressed; Futurism prized vigor and youth, but no sterilization or marriage policy is recorded.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: A movement glorifying war and violence would not hold forces to account for past killings; inferred, though the program also opposed the political police.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The program called for a strong technocratic state steering modernisation, not a minimal one.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Early Futurism was nationalist but not centred on race purity; Marinetti was reluctant about racial laws, so split; inferred.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: It glorified the strong, youth and war and scorned the weak and women; inferred from the manifesto's cult of strength.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Futurist politics was nationalist and set against internationalist revolution; inferred.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Marinetti celebrated Italian expansion and colonial war, so he would not call it a crime; inferred.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Its anti-clerical, anti-tradition stance favours one secular law over church-run family law; inferred.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Futurism was hostile to the Church but not concerned with conversion; inferred from its liberty-for-the-new attitude.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Sacred-animal taboos are the kind of inherited tradition Futurism wanted swept away; inferred.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The 1918 programme was anti-clerical and wanted the Church's influence out of public life, including schooling.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Futurists wanted a strong, armed nationalist state, not one withering away; inferred, since the idea is Marxist.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The manifesto glorifies bold leadership and action over deliberation; inferred.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: The manifesto scorns academies and received learning but never argues that truth is a product of power; inferred and split, consistent with the audit's answer on knowledge and power.

trade-surplus.rationale: The 1918 program and Marinetti's expansionism treat national strength and economic power as aims; a trade surplus is inferred from that nationalism.

population-transfer.rationale: Futurist nationalism and expansionism, with its glorification of war, makes forced removal of hostile groups an inferred fit, though the sources do not address it directly.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The manifesto glorifies war, aggression and violence as the world's only hygiene, so a ban on starting force is rejected.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The manifesto celebrates struggle, aggression and war between peoples as the source of vitality and renewal.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Futurism merged into early Fascism, which banned rival parties; inferred, as the Futurist program itself says nothing about outlawing parties.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: The movement prized dynamic action and national will over limits on rulers; inferred from its authoritarian drift, not stated.

separated-powers.rationale: The 1918 program wanted government by technically trained youth able to act decisively, and Futurists scorned institutional brakes; inferred.

vanguard-party.rationale: Futurism cast itself as an avant-garde minority of young artists and activists leading the masses; applying that to a party is inferred.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The 1918 program had redistributive elements (progressive tax, no inheritance) but the movement prized strength over the weak; adherents are split and the sources do not settle it.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Not addressed: the 1918 program targeted inheritance and wealth but said nothing on council housing sales.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Inferred: the 1918 program backed workers' agitation, yet futurists prized national discipline and later sat inside Fascism, which banned strikes.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Not addressed as a cause of poverty; Marinetti's expansionism cited Italian population pressure but the program blamed institutions and privilege.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Inferred: its intense Italian nationalism and glorification of the nation fit a shared-identity view of cohesion.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Inferred: the 1918 program wanted government by technically skilled youth, which rules out chance selection.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Inferred: the movement glorified violence and war and merged into Fascism, which suspended protections against internal enemies.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Not addressed: the program had no stated position on price ceilings.

party-controls-media.rationale: Not addressed: futurists were avant-garde provocateurs who also clashed with regime cultural control; adherents are split.

party-commands-army.rationale: Not addressed: the program proposed a volunteer army but no party command of it.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Inferred: the movement's strong Italian nationalism favours demanding long commitment before membership.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: The 1918 program set no pay rule for officeholders; not addressed.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Marinetti prized artistic individualism yet fused the party into disciplined early Fascism, so the question is split.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Futurism was fiercely nationalist and glorified the Italian nation, so shared sovereignty cuts against it.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Inferred from Marinetti joining Mussolini's strong-executive regime; the 1918 program itself favored a republic.

church-by-bishops.rationale: The Futurist Political Party was anti-clerical and sought to strip the church of influence, so it opposed an episcopal state church.

clerical-rule.rationale: Anti-clericalism was a defining plank of Futurist politics, which wanted priests out of public power.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: The manifesto glorified war and nationalism; Futurists urged Italy into the First World War and backed it.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Futurists attacked academies and museums and demanded total artistic freedom for the new, so moral censorship of art contradicts them.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Not addressed; the program favored a republic but said nothing on term limits, and Marinetti later accepted Mussolini's unlimited rule.

recall-officials.rationale: Inferred from the 1918 program's radical, anti-establishment democratic reforms; no recall provision is documented.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the aggressive nationalism and expansionism of the movement, which sat badly with giving up military commitments.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: The 1918 program taxed inheritance and wealth but said nothing on tenancy, so it is not addressed.

people-in-arms.rationale: The program backed a volunteer army and the movement glorified war, but it did not call for an armed citizenry in place of a professional force.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The manifesto glorifies cities, factories, speed and machines and rejects the past, so it prized urban modernity over country life.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Futurist nationalism was irredentist, demanding that Italian-speaking lands outside the Italian state be joined to it.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Futurists mocked professors and academies, yet the program put technically trained youth in government; not addressed directly.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Futurist nationalism assumed Italian cultural superiority and the glory of the nation over others.

death-penalty.rationale: Inferred from the glorification of violence and war; no stated position on capital punishment.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: The program favored women's political rights while the manifesto voiced scorn for woman, so the movement is split.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Futurism was anti-clerical and celebrated science and machines, so teaching creationism would be rejected.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Inferred from the movement's hostility to moralism and censorship of art; no stated position.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Not addressed; the movement was nationalist but its expansionist aims centered on territory rather than rules of citizenship.

minority-language-support.rationale: Inferred from its intense Italian nationalism, which favored a single national culture and language.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Inferred from its anti-clerical stance and rejection of religious authority in public life.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: The manifesto rejects tradition, convention and the past and celebrates youthful audacity and novelty.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Not addressed; the 1918 program was nationalist and anti-establishment but said nothing on foreign debt.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The 1918 program pairing independence-minded nationalism with progressive tax and abolished inheritance suggests economic change was expected; inferred.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Inferred from the anti-monarchist, anti-parliament 1918 program calling for a fresh start; the exact mechanism is not stated.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Futurists glorified authority, speed and nationalist ends over liberal procedure and later accommodated the Fascist state.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Inferred from aggressive nationalism and expansionism, which put national power ahead of duties to foreigners.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Anachronistic: inferred from the cult of national power, war and technology.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The program sought a government of technical youth in place of parliament; direct election is not mentioned, so inferred.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Inferred from the technocratic, state-steered modernization the program wanted over liberal institutional checks.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: The program and Marinetti's politics were expansionist and irredentist, claiming land rather than ceding it.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The program's progressive tax and ban on inheritance imply property is subject to the national interest; inferred.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Anachronistic: Marinetti joined Fascism and opposed Bolshevism, so he would likely have seen the USSR as socialist; inferred.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Futurism celebrated risk, speed and technology and scorned caution; inferred.

collective-defense.rationale: Nationalist Futurism preferred Italy deciding on its own; alliance obligations are inferred as unwelcome.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Italian expansionism in the 1918 program implies taking territory is acceptable; inferred.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The 1918 party program was anti-clerical and aimed at curbing the Church.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Futurists despised party politics and the monarchy, favoring a technical government of youth; a neutral symbol is inferred to be unwanted.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Glorification of war and aggressive nationalism imply force for national unity; inferred.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Strongly centralizing nationalism is inferred to oppose distinct regional systems.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The party was anti-monarchist and anti-clerical, rejecting sacred rule.

flat-income-tax.rationale: The 1918 program called for progressive taxation, opposing a flat tax.

character-from-environment.rationale: Futurist belief in remaking people through modern life is inferred to stress circumstances.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Marinetti accommodated the Fascist regime, and strong rulers are inferred to stand above old law.

space-expansion.rationale: Celebration of technology and expansion is inferred to favor spreading into space.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Futurism rejected inherited institutions and favored a technical government of youth; a balanced old-style constitution is inferred as unwanted.

leader-cult.rationale: Marinetti backed Mussolini and Futurism glorified strong leaders; inferred rather than stated.

equal-parenting.rationale: The 1918 program had state-funded child-rearing and Futurism scorned family; inferred.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Marinetti rejected Bolshevik collectivism and married futurism to nationalism, so class-struggle doctrine is rejected; inferred.

land-redistribution.rationale: The 1918 program included land reclamation for war veterans, a modest land-to-people plank.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Futurists campaigned for Italian irredentism against Austria-Hungary and the party program was expansionist.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The 1918 program was anti-clerical and the movement scorned the 'religion of the past'.

women-must-cover.rationale: Anti-clerical and anti-moralist, so religious dress mandates are inferred as rejected.

common-currency.rationale: Intense Italian nationalism implies preference for a national currency; inferred.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Nationalism was Italy-centred; cross-border kin unions are inferred as foreign to it.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The 1918 program was anti-monarchist and sought to abolish inheritance and privilege.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Marinetti's nationalism and glorification of war and Italian colonial expansion imply support for Italian rule abroad; inferred rather than stated as a doctrine.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from nationalist, anti-egalitarian views with no concern for group preferences.

public-money-creation.rationale: Not addressed in the manifesto or party program; no inference is possible either way.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The party program mixed nationalism with radical social proposals and did not stake a position on capitalism's long-run stability.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Futurism glorified war and expansion and tied itself to Italian nationalism and imperial claims, including Roman heritage and Mediterranean influence.

delink-world-market.rationale: Not addressed; Futurist autarkic nationalism and industrial modernisation pull in different directions.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Not addressed by Futurist sources; inferred that it would not use such a class-based framing.

minority-veto.rationale: Inferred from the manifesto's contempt for consensus and its glorification of aggression and the decisive act.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Inferred from the party's revolutionary anti-monarchist stance; no doctrine on legal resistance is given.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Inferred from the manifesto's contempt for pity and sentimentality; animals not addressed.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred: Futurism celebrated mastery over nature and did not question animal use.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Inferred from the manifesto's scorn for the weak and for tradition; paternal duty is not stated.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The founding manifesto glorifies action, speed and war, and scorns passive contemplation.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Inferred: Futurists embraced mass media and propaganda as tools, not as pacifiers; no theory of pacification is stated.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Not addressed as a theory; Futurists worked inside regime institutions but did not theorize consent.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Inferred from its aggressive nationalism and expansionism; not a dependency theory.

native-born-offices.rationale: Inferred from the 1918 program's intense Italian nationalism; not stated for offices.

party-own-road.rationale: Not addressed; Futurism was a nationalist movement, not a communist or socialist party doctrine.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Inferred from its nationalism and its expansionist program that Italy should rely on its own strength.

return-lost-territory.rationale: The 1918 program and Marinetti's nationalism were irredentist and expansionist, demanding Trento, Trieste and other lands.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred from its Italian nationalism and elitist outlook; not addressed.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Futurism merged into early Fascism and stayed loosely tied to the regime until 1944, so anti-fascism as a founding value is opposed.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Inferred: Marinetti allied with Fascism and was fiercely anti-communist; equating the two is not stated.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Not addressed; an Italian movement with no documented view of American history.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: The founding manifesto calls for destroying museums, libraries and the cult of the past.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Inferred from the manifesto's virile, aggressive ethos; not addressed.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Inferred from the manifesto's scorn for woman and its masculinist ethos.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Inferred from its nationalism and rejection of liberal universalism; not stated.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Inferred from the manifesto's glorification of war and the army; the guardian-of-constitution role is not stated.

paid-care-work.rationale: The 1918 program included state-funded child-rearing, but the sources do not address paying for unpaid domestic work.

filial-duty.rationale: Inferred from the manifesto's rejection of the past and its institutions; filial duty is not addressed.

office-by-exam.rationale: The 1918 program favored a government of technically skilled youth over traditional politicians.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Inferred from the intense nationalism described in the reference sources.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred from the anti-clerical, anti-traditional stance of the 1918 program; not stated directly.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Inferred from Marinetti's contempt for parliaments and later merger into Fascism.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Inferred from the program's state-centred social measures; pensions are not discussed.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Inferred from the program's progressive taxation and abolition of inheritance, which weaken private holdings, not from any stated land policy.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Inferred from the movement's scorn for parliamentary politics and later alignment with Fascism.

single-official-language.rationale: Inferred from the nationalist, expansionist program; language policy is not discussed.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the aggressive nationalism of the program; not stated directly.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Inferred from the movement's nationalism and contempt for egalitarian reform; the issue is anachronistic.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Inferred from the glorification of speed, machines and heroism over comfort; consumerism is not addressed.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Inferred from the program's expansionism and glorification of war.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Inferred from the program's expansionism and the movement's exaltation of national power.

corporate-influence.rationale: Not addressed; the 1918 program targeted elites and old institutions but not lobbying specifically.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred from the intense nationalism and national sovereignty emphasis of the movement.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: The 1918 program included state-funded child-rearing, and Marinetti prized national expansion and population; inferred.

residents-only-property.rationale: Not addressed; nationalist but without a stated position on local property limits.

job-guarantee.rationale: The 1918 program is not shown to include a job guarantee; no clear position.

democratic-peace.rationale: Marinetti glorified war and expansion, which sits against the idea that spreading democracy brings peace.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Marinetti's defiance of established institutions and law suggests no deference to law as such; inferred.

non-intervention.rationale: Futurism celebrated war and expansionism and backed force without restraint on national grounds.

industrial-unions.rationale: Not addressed; later aligned with Fascist corporatism, but no clear position on union form.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Not addressed; the movement's nationalism was not defined by a minority conspiracy narrative.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The 1918 program was anti-clerical and attacked traditional institutions; inferred an opposition to church-bound marriage.

public-access-to-information.rationale: A vanguard of technical youth ruling with broad powers is at odds with open access; inferred.

local-production.rationale: Futurism celebrated speed, machines and industry, and disdained rural and local traditional life.

informal-organisation.rationale: Futurists formed a party and then merged into the Fascist movement, which was centralised and hierarchical.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Futurism was strongly nationalist and rejected deference to outside bodies; national interest comes first.

religious-nation.rationale: The 1918 program was anti-clerical and the movement scorned tradition and the Church.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Inferred: Futurism wanted Italy itself to lead and rejected deference to the past and established powers, so ritual tribute is alien to it.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Inferred from the 1918 programme's centralised national state and hostility to local particularism.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The 1918 programme favoured progressive tax and an end to inheritance but not common ownership of the means of production.

defeat-communism.rationale: Inferred: Marinetti's nationalism and fascist ties were hostile to Bolshevism, though the sources do not state a crusade against communism.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Not addressed; the 1918 programme set no rule on who delivers public services.

religion-illusion.rationale: Inferred from the party's anti-clerical programme, though its reasoning was nationalist rather than a materialist theory of religion.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Futurists celebrated modern industry and machines and wanted to break with the agrarian past, which is close to this claim.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The 1909 manifesto declares scorn for woman, and the movement did not tie equality to economic change.

socialized-care.rationale: The 1918 programme included state-funded child-rearing, which is close to public provision of care.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Inferred from Futurism's intense nationalism; the sources do not record a specific campaign on loanwords.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred from aggressive nationalism and contempt for restraint by past institutions.

cooperative-communities.rationale: The programme's centralised technocratic state and rejection of the past leave no place for small communal communities.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred from the programme's expansionist nationalism; the sources do not mention settlement policy.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The 1918 party was neither liberal-capitalist nor socialist, and Marinetti later fitted into Fascism's claim of a distinct course.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Marinetti's nationalism and expansionism rested on Italian claims to territory, but he scorned the past; inferred and mixed.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Futurism ended in 1944 and the sources do not address it; Marinetti's links to Fascism make a firm answer uncertain, so mild disagreement is inferred.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Not addressed; Futurists scorned conventional morality, though Marinetti's cult of virility makes it uncertain; inferred.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The movement glorified aggression and violence and merged into early Fascism, though the 1918 programme envisaged government by technical youth and was anti-monarchist.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The 1918 programme was anti-clerical and the movement attacked the Church and tradition.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Marinetti and the 1918 programme advocated Italian expansionism and imperial growth.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Religious-law war duty is outside this movement, which was anti-clerical, though it admired war; inferred.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: The movement was anti-clerical and secular, and wanted no religious test for rulers.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The 1918 programme called for government by technical youth in place of parliament, rejecting rule by ordinary politicians; direct participation is not stated.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The movement held a contemptuous view of women in 1909 and gave no support to anti-oppression framings.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Not addressed; the movement's cult of masculinity points to disagreement, inferred.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not addressed; the cult of speed, youth and contempt for weakness suggests agreement, inferred.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Futurists wanted to sweep away the old order and combined nationalist and revolutionary-left elements, as the Wikipedia article on the Futurist party notes; inferred.

alienated-labor.rationale: Futurists celebrated machines, factories and industrial work and did not use an alienation critique; inferred.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Not addressed; Marinetti's nationalism and colonial expansion could cut either way, and he was equally contemptuous of all religion.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The movement was anti-clerical and demanded breaking with tradition, with authority resting on national will and youth.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: The anti-clerical 1918 programme implies that religious symbols have no place in state institutions; inferred.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Anachronistic; the movement's attitudes to women and aggressive masculinity point to disagreement, inferred.

social-market-economy.rationale: The 1918 programme mixed progressive taxation and no inheritance with nationalism and industry; neither a laissez-faire nor a social-market model is stated.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The 1909 manifesto glorifies war as the world's only hygiene, and the programme called for a volunteer army.

rich-first.rationale: The 1918 programme set progressive tax and ended inheritance, but also backed industrial growth; not addressed in these terms.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: The movement was interventionist and pushed Italy into the First World War, so staying out of conflicts is rejected; inferred.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Futurism was anti-monarchist and attacked inherited institutions, and the 1918 program called for abolishing the monarchy.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: The 1918 program had anti-bourgeois economic planks but no known position on mutual credit; split by inference.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Intense Italian nationalism implies resisting foreign dictates, though Futurists wrote little on finance; inferred.

property-franchise.rationale: The 1918 program called for universal suffrage including women, so a property qualification conflicts, though Marinetti disdained parliamentary voting.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Futurism glorified scorn for women and called for nature's conquest by machines, so the link is rejected; inferred from the manifesto.

reification.rationale: Futurists were not socialist theorists and celebrated industry, so the claim is not part of its thought; inferred.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The 1918 program was anti-bourgeois and sought a break from old elites, but press freedom was not framed this way.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Futurism glorified action and violence over legal process and valued the strong leader, so rule by standing law is opposed; inferred.

racial-franchise.rationale: Futurism was ethnic-nationalist in Italy's favour, though the 1918 program sought universal suffrage; leaning agree, inferred.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic; Futurists celebrated new technology of communication, but this is not a stated position.

open-government-data.rationale: Anachronistic and not stated in the sources; split by inference.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Futurism's 1918 program was anti-clerical and it attacked the Church, so religious marriage restrictions are inferred as opposed.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Futurist nationalism was not primarily religious, and later Fascist racial laws drew mixed Futurist responses; inferred, split.

citizens-assembly.rationale: The 1918 Futurist programme wanted parliament abolished and government by technical and expert bodies and strong action, not deliberation by ordinary citizens chosen by lot (inferred).

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Futurists were fiercely anticlerical and wanted the Church's weight removed rather than its doctrine rethought, so they would reject both the reform and the preservation framing (inferred).

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The 1918 program called for heavy taxation of capital and war profits, implying hostility to concentrated wealth, though from nationalist rather than liberty-based grounds.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Marinetti scorned bourgeois morality but glorified a virile warrior cult; nothing in the sources settles gay service, so this is split.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The program was anti-clerical and wanted the Church's influence curbed, but it sought secularisation, not state-promoted atheism; inferred from its anti-clerical planks.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Futurism celebrated war, violence and national strength, so dissolving police and prisons runs against it; inferred from the manifesto's cult of force.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: A strongly nationalist, centralising movement would not hand executive power to rival communities; inferred from its nationalism.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The program favoured state-run social measures such as state-funded child-rearing, not reliance on private charity.

term-limits.rationale: Futurists wanted to push out the old political class and replace it with youth; term limits fit that, though the program does not state them.

vote-delegation.rationale: The program wanted to replace parliament with technical bodies and strong leadership, not a revocable proxy system; inferred.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: The movement exalted risk, speed and war and had no concern for long-run human survival as a policy goal; inferred from the manifesto.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Futurists were anti-clerical and backed women's suffrage, but there is no stated view on women's religious offices.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The 1918 program pushed women's rights such as the vote and attacked bourgeois family institutions, so ending husbandly authority fits; inferred.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred from Futurism's intense Italian nationalism and glorification of patriotism.

rent-control.rationale: Not addressed; the 1918 program is silent on housing.

abolish-ip.rationale: Not addressed; Futurists scorned the past but the program is silent on intellectual property.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred from the celebration of youth, discipline and war and the 1918 program's rule by young technicians.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from nationalist insistence on Italian independence of action.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the nationalist stress on national sovereignty and expansion.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Not addressed; the sources never discuss genocide recognition.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The 1918 program called for a progressive tax and abolition of inheritance, which curbs wealth from ownership.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The 1909 manifesto glorifies war, violence and aggression as the world's only hygiene.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Inferred from Futurism's rejection of the past and tradition as a model for the present.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the movement's contempt for woman and its macho outlook.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the movement's scorn for feminism and women's claims.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred from the manifesto's glorification of dying in war for the fatherland, though Futurists were anti-clerical.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: The movement was anti-clerical and worshipped machines and speed rather than spiritual forces.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Inferred from expansionist nationalism that wanted the nation gathered under a strong state.

culture-before-state.rationale: Futurists sought both a cultural break with the past and a political party, so no clear order follows.

god-not-male.rationale: Anachronistic; anti-clerical but scornful of women, so no clear stance.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred from scorn for woman and the sacred; Futurists would not judge texts by women's humanity.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Inferred from Italian nationalism; not addressed directly.

independent-unions.rationale: Futurists merged into Fascism and the 1918 party program was nationalist with state-led aims, so independent unions were not a priority.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The 1918 program talked of a technical, producer-led state but Futurism's politics were elitist and nationalist; inferred.

local-essentials-public.rationale: The 1918 party program included nationalisation of some assets, but nothing specific on local services.

second-chamber.rationale: The 1918 program sought to replace parliament with a technical government; inferred opposition to a second chamber.

municipal-property.rationale: Not addressed directly; the party favoured state-led expropriation and a nationalist state rather than local ownership.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Futurism despised localism and tradition and exalted the nation-state; inferred.

family-wage.rationale: Not addressed; the 1918 program had social welfare items, but nothing on the family wage.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Futurism celebrated speed and progress, so faster approvals fit; anachronistic, inferred.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: The movement's glorification of science, youth and overcoming limits fits ageing research; anachronistic, inferred.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Anachronistic; Futurism celebrated technology but also the strong nationalist state.

online-anonymity.rationale: Anachronistic; not addressed in the sources.

person-over-state.rationale: Futurists exalted the nation and violence and merged into Fascism, which treated persons as subordinate to the state.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Futurism proclaimed machines and speed and was anti-clerical, rejecting spiritualism; the 1918 party was anti-clerical.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Not addressed; Italian nationalism favoured a unified state, but the 1918 program is silent on regions.

gm-crops.rationale: Anachronistic; the movement's enthusiasm for technology suggests support.

dense-cities.rationale: Futurism loved the modern industrial city and its speed; inferred from Marinetti's manifesto praising cities, factories and crowds.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Futurism was an Italian nationalist movement, not a racial-group one; inferred as split.

racial-pride.rationale: Marinetti's intense nationalism and pride in Italy's people and greatness is central, though framed as national not racial.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: The manifesto glorifies war as the world's only hygiene and Futurists agitated for Italy's entry into WWI and conquest.

missingStatements.text: Museums, libraries and other inherited cultural institutions should be sacrificed if they hold back new creation.
missingStatements.rationale: The manifesto vows to destroy museums, libraries and academies.

missingStatements.text: Society should speed up technological change even if it disrupts existing institutions.
missingStatements.rationale: Marinetti declares the beauty of speed as the new beauty.

notes: The movement changed over time: the 1918-1920 program was radical and anti-establishment, while later Futurists accommodated the Fascist state, and Russian Futurists leaned communist. Many answers are inferred because Futurism was an artistic movement with only a brief political program.
